questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Assume the passenger has ridden a motorcycle before.
Not assume they have ridden before. Explain what they need to do.
Not explain anything since they are just a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume they have ridden before. Explain what they need to do.
questions.explanation: Passengers need to know how to ride safely. Never assume they know what to do. Give them clear instructions before every ride.

questions.question: For motorcycle safety, you should:

options.text: Assume everything on your motorcycle works properly.
Check your motorcycle before every ride.
Check your motorcycle once a month.
Check your motorcycle twice a week.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your motorcycle before every ride.
questions.explanation: Even small problems can be serious on a motorcycle. Check your motorcycle carefully before every ride.

questions.question: If you feel tired while riding, you should:

options.text: Keep riding and try to stay awake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest.
questions.explanation: Do not ride when you are tired. On long trips, stop and rest at least every two hours to prevent fatigue.

questions.question: When braking, you should use:

options.text: One brake at a time, never both together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both brakes together.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes at the same time. This gives you the best stopping power.

questions.question: A way to reduce crash risk is to:

options.text: Signal your movements to other drivers.
Ride in spots where others cannot see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal your movements to other drivers.
questions.explanation: Be visible to others. Use your signals and brake light. Position yourself in the lane so others can see you. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have:

options.text: A front brake and a rear brake.
Three brakes: front, rear, and emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: A front brake and a rear brake.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have two brakes. One controls the front wheel and one controls the rear wheel.

questions.question: When choosing a protective jacket or pants, look for:
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather material.
questions.explanation: Wear long pants and a jacket to cover your arms and legs. Leather provides the best protection.

questions.question: The body eliminates almost ______ of alcohol per hour.
questions.correctAnswerText: One drink
questions.explanation: Your body can process about one drink per hour on average.

questions.question: During a pre-ride check, make sure that:

options.text: The brakes make a loud squeaking sound.
The brakes create friction with the steering.
Each brake can hold the motorcycle.
Only the rear brake can hold the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each brake can hold the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Test each brake lever before every ride. Make sure it feels firm and stops the motorcycle when fully applied.

questions.question: Which type of clothing helps other drivers see you?
questions.correctAnswerText: Reflective clothes
questions.explanation: Wear bright, reflective clothing so other drivers can see you and your motorcycle.

questions.question: To reduce your risk of having an accident, you should:

options.text: Ride within one foot of the vehicle in front of you.
Signal only when you want to.
Stay alert and be ready to act to avoid a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay alert and be ready to act to avoid a crash.
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, be visible to other drivers. Use your signals, brake lights, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space between you and other vehicles. Always look ahead, behind, and to the sides of your motorcycle.

questions.question: Riding at night is usually:

options.text: Easier than riding during the day because you can see other vehicles' lights better.
Harder than riding during the day because visibility is reduced.
Less distracting than riding during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder than riding during the day because visibility is reduced.
questions.explanation: Riding at night is more challenging because you cannot see as well and other drivers cannot see you as easily. Without natural light and shadows, it is harder to judge how far away things are.

questions.question: The best gear to wear when you ride is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Any gear that protects you.
questions.explanation: Wear gear that protects you while riding. This includes a DOT-approved helmet, eye or face protection, and protective clothing.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol, you should:

options.text: Decide whether you can ride safely based on how you feel after drinking.
Set a drinking limit before drinking so you can still ride safely.
Not worry about your riding if you feel fine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not ride.
questions.explanation: The safest choice is to not ride after drinking any alcohol. Even small amounts of alcohol can reduce your riding ability.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle:

options.text: You may speed up past the limit until you finish passing.
You may ignore "No passing zone" markings if you started passing in a legal zone.
You may pass on the shoulder.
You must stay within the speed limit and pass only in legal passing zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stay within the speed limit and pass only in legal passing zones.
questions.explanation: You must obey the speed limit while passing. Only pass where it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT protective clothing for a motorcyclist?
questions.correctAnswerText: A stocking cap
questions.explanation: Wear protective clothing when riding. This includes sturdy jackets and pants that cover your arms and legs, boots or heavy shoes that support your ankles, and sturdy gloves.

questions.question: Motorcycles:

options.text: Do not have blind spots because they are small.
Have blind spots, but they are small enough not to worry about.
Have blind spots that you should regularly check.
Are too small to have blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots that you should regularly check.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like other vehicles. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Make head checks a regular part of scanning the road.

questions.question: Riding gloves are often:
questions.correctAnswerText: Made of leather.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riding gloves are usually made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders should wear shoes with soles that:
questions.correctAnswerText: Are hard, durable, and slip-resistant.
questions.explanation: Choose boots or shoes that are high and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles. Pick footwear with soles made of hard, durable, slip-resistant material.

questions.question: What is often found in the center of the lane?
questions.correctAnswerText: An oily or greasy strip
questions.explanation: Car drippings form an oily strip in the center of each lane. It is usually safe for a motorcycle to ride on the center strip unless the road is wet.

questions.question: Under Oregon law, what is required for a motorcycle headlight?

options.text: The headlight must only be on between 7 p.m. and 7 a.m.
The headlight must be on whenever the motorcycle is running.
A motorcycle may have four lights on the front.

questions.correctAnswerText: The headlight must be on whenever the motorcycle is running.
questions.explanation: Oregon law requires motorcycle headlights to be on at all times while riding. Using your headlight helps other drivers see you.

questions.question: What happens when you take a corner too fast?

options.text: You may cross into another lane.
It is better than going too slowly.
You will usually stay in your lane.
It is safe because motorcycles are smaller than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross into another lane.
questions.explanation: Taking a corner too fast can cause you to cross into another lane or go off the road. Slow down before you turn or take a curve.

questions.question: Where should you get information about your motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: The owner's manual.
questions.explanation: Your owner's manual is the best source for information about your specific motorcycle. It includes details about how your motorcycle works and how to maintain it.

questions.question: What type of boots or shoes should you wear when riding?

options.text: Shoes with long laces that hang loose.
Boots that cover and support your ankles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Boots that cover and support your ankles.
questions.explanation: Wear tall, sturdy boots or heavy shoes that cover and support your ankles. Use low heels so they won't catch on things. Tuck in long laces so they don't get caught in the motorcycle.

questions.question: When your turn is obvious, should you use a turn signal?

options.text: No, you do not need to use one.
Yes, you should always use one.
Only if there are pedestrians nearby.
Only if you are at a stop light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, you should always use one.
questions.explanation: Always use a turn signal when you turn or change lanes, even if you think it is obvious. Other vehicles may be near you that you cannot see. Signals are always important for safety.
